title: Soft Reserve Scaling and Tenancy Controls - PRD (sketch)
content:
Context and problem

We sell Dedicated capacity to customers who need predictable throughput and strong data isolation. A recurring ask is: allow customers to keep predictable baseline capacity while permitting controlled, short-term bursts above their committed baseline to absorb traffic spikes. Operators also need clearer tenancy/isolation primitives so we can balance utilization across reserved pools but avoid noisy-neighbor incidents and unexpected evictions.

We currently have a fairly rigid reserved model (fixed pools, hard caps, manual ops for bursts) which leads to:
- Over-provisioning by customers to tolerate spikes
- Manual interventions by SRE during large transient loads
- Hard tradeoffs between utilization and strict isolation (hard-evict vs reserved dead space)

Goal

Design a product feature set (soft-reserve scaling + tenancy controls) that enables:
1) Predictable baseline SLOs for reserved customers (latency/throughput)
2) Controlled elastic bursting above baseline for short periods with clear billing implications
3) Configurable isolation levels per reservation to tune eviction behavior, headroom, and QoS
4) Operator-visible policies and metrics so SRE can automate remediation and set safe cluster-level defaults
5) Minimal changes to onboarding, billing, and our console UX while preserving security/compliance controls for Private/Dedicated customers

Non-goals

- Replacing Dedicated’s billing model entirely (we will augment with burst billing but keep reserve + overage model)
- Supporting unlimited bursting without bounds
- Complex per-request QoS tokens in this phase (keep to pool-level controls)

User personas and key user stories

- Platform engineer at a fintech startup: "I want our dedicated pool to guarantee 95th-pct latency for normal traffic and allow 10% soft-burst capacity for periodic batch jobs, billed only when used."
- SRE: "I want automated policies that prevent noisy tenants from consuming all capacity and evict/shape according to business impact levels."
- Account manager / customer success: "I need clear explanations for customers about how bursts are metered and how isolation level affects cost and eviction risk."

High-level proposal

Introduce three complementary constructs:
1) Soft Reserve: an elastic headroom layer attached to a reservation that can be consumed when spare capacity exists. Consumption is time-limited and charged at a premium over baseline reserved units.
2) Tenancy Isolation Levels: a small set of predefined profiles (Strict, Balanced, Economical) that define eviction priority, maximum burst ratio, preemption grace period, and how KV cache/k-cache is shared.
3) Cluster Fairness Policy & Global Headroom Pool: cluster-level throttles and a managed global headroom pool that can be used to satisfy soft reserve across reservations while protecting critical customers.

Soft Reserve details

- Parameters per reservation: baseline_capacity (gpus/slots), soft_ratio (e.g., 0.1 for 10% extra), soft_burst_duration (max continuous seconds/minutes allowed), per_unit_burst_price_multiplier (1.5x baseline rate).
- Example: baseline 10 units, soft_ratio 0.2 => up to +2 units for bursts. Bursts capped to 2 units sustained up to soft_burst_duration (e.g., 15 minutes).
- Metering granularity: per-minute consumption reporting; billing uses a blended model: baseline billed as committed; soft units billed only for minutes consumed at premium rate.
- Exhaustion behavior: if cluster headroom exhausted or higher-priority reservations need capacity, soft units are reclaimed according to tenancy isolation policy (see below). Reclaims attempt graceful drain (seconds of SIGTERM-equivalent), then preempt.

Tenancy isolation levels (operator-visible profiles)

Profile: Strict
- Eviction priority: lowest (least likely to be evicted)
- Max burst_ratio: 0.05 (small bursts only)
- Graceful reclaim window: 120s
- KV cache isolation: per-tenant strike isolation (no sharing)
- Use cases: regulated customers, high-SLA financial workloads

Profile: Balanced
- Eviction priority: medium
- Max burst_ratio: 0.2
- Graceful reclaim window: 60s
- KV cache isolation: soft share with sticky prefixes
- Use cases: typical SaaS customers who want some elasticity with decent guarantees

Profile: Economical
- Eviction priority: high (more likely to be reclaimed)
- Max burst_ratio: 0.5
- Graceful reclaim window: 20s
- KV cache isolation: best-effort share, no guarantees
- Use cases: dev/staging, cost-sensitive teams

Cluster-level safeguards

- Global Headroom Pool: a cluster-managed reserve (configurable percent of cluster capacity) that feeds soft reserves. Headroom policy tracks consumption and prevents runaway burst usage.
- Per-service throttles: routes or model groups can be temporarily throttled when cluster-level soft usage exceeds threshold.
- Emergency protective mode: when cluster saturation approaches critical levels, auto-disable soft reserves across non-strict tenants, with console alerting and email to account owners.

Operator and console UX

- Reservation creation UI: new fields for Soft Reserve (on/off), soft_ratio slider, burst price preview, and tenancy profile selector.
- Dashboard: per-reservation live chart showing baseline vs soft consumption, reclaim events, and cost-to-date attributable to bursts.
- Policy API: existing reservation API extended with fields: soft_reserve: true/false, soft_ratio, soft_burst_duration_seconds, tenancy_profile.

API sketch (JSON-like in text)
- PATCH /reservations/:id { "soft_reserve": true, "soft_ratio": 0.2, "soft_burst_duration_seconds": 900, "tenancy_profile": "balanced" }
- GET /reservations/:id/usage -> returns baseline_consumed_min, soft_consumed_min, soft_reclaims

Metrics and SLOs to track

- SoftConsumptionPct (per-reservation, per-cluster)
- SoftReclaims (count, reason)
- TimeToReclaim (median)
- BaselineLatencyP95 under burst events
- BurstCostDelta (currency) per billing interval

Billing implications

- Billing will show line items: committed_capacity, soft_burst_minutes, burst_rate_multiplier. Customer-visible estimate in Console before enabling.
- For enterprise contracts we will offer soft-reserve bundles (e.g., monthly soft-credit pool) and negotiation knobs for lower burst multipliers.

Operational runbooks (draft)

- Normal soft reclaim: API signals workload to drain, allow grace window. If still active, preempt. Report as 'soft_reclaim_success' or 'soft_reclaim_force_eviction'.
- When cluster headroom depleted: shift low-priority tenants to limited mode; send account owner notifications; escalate to on-call if >N reclaims in M minutes.
- Rollback: console toggle to globally disable soft reserve on a cluster.

Rollout plan

Phase 0 (canary, 2 weeks)
- Implement simple soft_reserve in one cluster with Economical and Balanced profiles. Manual ops guardrails. Invite 2 pilot customers.
Phase 1 (regional roll)
- Add Strict profile, billing line items, console UI. Expand pilots to 10 customers.
Phase 2 (GA)
- Global headroom pool, tuning heuristics, public docs and pricing page updates. Offer soft-reserve bundles for enterprise customers.

Open questions / tradeoffs

- Pricing model sensitivity: what premium is acceptable? We should A/B with 1.25x, 1.5x, 2x multipliers for burst units.
- Per-request vs pool-level QoS: later we could add token buckets per route to avoid evicting entire reservations during spikes.
- Long-running state: if customers continually use soft reserve, do we convert to committed capacity automatically? We should consider a threshold-based auto-convert flow (opt-in).
- Complexity for sales/cs: how to explain isolation profiles simply? Need clear one-pagers and decision matrix.

Next steps (immediate)

- Product: finalize tenancy_profile definitions and default values (owner: Aisha) by EOD Nov 20.
- Eng: prototype API shape and cluster reclaim hook (owner: Samir) — spike this week.
- Billing: propose initial burst multiplier options and how to show estimate in console (owner: Elena).
- SRE: draft emergency protective-mode runbook and thresholds (owner: Connor).

Notes to self / rough ideas

- Consider 'soft credits' monthly for startups — prevents surprise bills and can be upsell path.
- Cache isolation knobs are surprisingly sensitive for LLM workloads; need experiments to quantify performance delta between strict and shared cache.
- Make sure Private deployments have equivalent knobs but default to stricter profiles for compliance customers.

This doc is a working sketch — plenty of details to iterate (billing contract language, exact reclaim sequencing, and UI copy). Welcome feedback in the comments or the linked PROD-304 ticket.
